change.title: Include one CP/M-80 module in every migration package
change.reason: The author identifies the hardware module as crucial to this offering. Supply one unconditionally; retain application qualification without using it as a condition for whether the module is included. This resolves the CP/M module finding from the earlier quantity discussion. Its cable finding is addressed by the separate fixed-cable proposal.

supply_condition.description: Only where application qualification requires the CP/M-80 hardware module

after.name: Move from CP/M to Artemis
after.description: CP/M-to-Artemis migration package supplying one Artemis CP/M-80 hardware module as a required component. Application compatibility still requires qualification.

composition_history.description: Migration package with one included Artemis CP/M-80 hardware module

change.title: Define software memory and storage limits
change.reason: Provide measured or explicitly selected RAM/ROM budgets per edition and platform, distinguishing installed memory from working set and ROM occupancy.

before.name: Logix Aurelia 16 KB RAM expansion card
before.description: Optional 16 KB RAM card occupying one Plug and Execute expansion slot. On Aurelia it increases installed RAM from 48 KB to 64 KB. The mapper exposes its four 4 KB pages at B000–EFFF in the normal application view; ROM and video RAM can temporarily overlay those pages without erasing their contents.

memory_mapping.configuration: Firmware discovers the card at startup and maps its pages; no manual address switches.
memory_mapping.system_workspace: The existing 4 KB common system RAM remains at F000–FFFF; the card adds 16 KB to lower RAM.
memory_mapping.service_calls: The common-memory runtime saves the RAM mapping, selects ROM/video RAM for a service and restores the card pages before returning.
memory_mapping.installation: Install with power off, then restart so firmware can discover and test the card.
memory_mapping.application_memory: Lower RAM rises from 44 KB to 60 KB, before other system and workspace reservations.

physical_population.refresh_owner: Host memory controller must refresh the card even while its pages are overlaid; exact interface pending.

adapter_requirements.buffer_policy: Local adapter RAM, additional to host system RAM. Partition transmit/receive buffers and metadata; freeze maximum frame length and IP MTU to fit complete frames before implementation. Physical RAM chip count remains unresolved.
adapter_requirements.flow_control: Grant unicast only when the destination advertises credit for a complete frame; reserve that credit until completion. Broadcast requires credit from all intended admitted receivers. Timeouts revoke stale credits; bounded queues and retry/error reporting prevent indefinite blocking. Use flow control first for receiver pressure, not automatic rate changes.
adapter_requirements.host_service: No per-byte interrupt requirement. Aurelia at 250 kbit/s has 128 CPU clocks per raw byte at 4 MHz; Aurelia+ at 500 kbit/s has 96 at 6 MHz. Validate worst-case service latency. A persistently slow host may advertise a lower configured ceiling.

adapter_requirements.flow_control: Grant unicast only when the destination advertises credit for a complete frame; reserve that credit until completion. Broadcast requires credit from all intended admitted receivers. Timeouts revoke stale credits; bounded queues and retry/error reporting prevent indefinite blocking. Use flow control first for receiver pressure, not automatic rate changes.
adapter_requirements.host_service: No per-byte interrupt requirement. Aurelia at 250 kbit/s has 128 CPU clocks per raw byte at 4 MHz; Aurelia+ at 500 kbit/s has 96 at 6 MHz. Validate worst-case service latency. A persistently slow host may advertise a lower configured ceiling.

before.name: Logix Artemis 32 KiB professional video card
before.description: Logix Artemis 32 KiB professional video card

specification.mode_discovery: Enumerate controller modes intersected with identified or configured monitor raster capabilities and available buffering/sprite allocations. Reject unsupported downscaling.

memory_layout.mode_exclusivity: Text/font and bitmap allocations are alternative uses of 32 KiB display DRAM. Exclusive 1 KiB sprite SRAM is available in every mode.
memory_layout.font_policy: One shared 256-glyph bank per mode. Font allocation 2048 bytes at 8×8, 4096 at 8×16 or 8×10 (16-byte glyph stride). Font writes affect both pages.
memory_layout.page_flip: Latch selected page during vertical blank; drawing throughput is not guaranteed by double buffering.

display_memory.organization: 16K × 16 bits; ordinary external DRAM, independent display refresh sequencer.

pixel_buffer.location: On video ASIC; SRAM banks with page ownership latches
pixel_buffer.policy: Eight-pixel parallel renderer fills free pages; independent clocked serializer drains ready pages. Two pages per 640-pixel line; prefill before active display; never overwrite displaying pages. Underflow blanks pixels, preserves sync and sets sticky fault.
pixel_buffer.physical_organization: Each 160-byte bank is 40 words × 32 bits. Load eight 4-bit pixels into a separate 32-bit serializer latch every eight dot clocks, then shift at 21.504 MHz. SRAM array reads run at 2.688 MHz, not one read per dot; filler and drain use different banks.

character_row_cache.purpose: Current and next 80-column character/attribute row; separate from 640-byte pixel FIFO.

timing_budget.qualification: At 250 ns conservative DRAM cycle, 80 glyph fetches consume 20 microseconds per active line; 160-byte row prefetch amortizes across 8/10/16 scanlines. Two row caches and 16-bit reads cover text-row transitions. Verify sprites, refresh and bounded host/DMA slots together at voltage/temperature corners; no guaranteed maximum CPU upload rate.

specification.arbitration: Card-local sequencer arbitrates display fetch and deadline-reserved independent DRAM refresh before bounded host/DMA transfers with READY. Sprite SRAM has its own 8-bit bus. System DMA/MMU remain dedicated host components; the card does not replace system-memory refresh.
specification.monitor_policy: Read capability descriptor before enabling sync. Mono Pro accepts only raster_640_400; integer-scale legacy modes. Old monitors retain their advertised 200-line raster(s), never 640×400. Native 400-line modes require Mono Pro; new 200-line bitmap modes also work on capable older displays. This is display-mode/API compatibility, not Z80 binary compatibility.

assembly_requirements.description: Engineering baseline; electrical qualification, routing and supplier quotes pending.

requirements.description: Dedicated slot; powered-off replacement only; host interface, power rails and signal integrity require qualification.
Qualification pending.

specification.mode_discovery: Enumerate controller modes intersected with identified or configured monitor raster capabilities and available buffering/sprite allocations. Reject unsupported downscaling.

memory_layout.mode_exclusivity: With palette-list mode enabled reserve 0xFA00–0xFFFF (1536 bytes); framebuffer/text/font allocations use 0x0000–0xF9FF. Text/font and bitmap layouts remain exclusive. Five sprites retain separate 1 KiB SRAM.
memory_layout.font_policy: One shared 256-glyph bank per mode. Font allocation 2048 bytes at 8×8, 4096 at 8×16 or 8×10 (16-byte glyph stride). Font writes affect both pages.
memory_layout.page_flip: Latch selected page during vertical blank; drawing throughput is not guaranteed by double buffering.

display_memory.organization: Two 16K x 16-bit banks; ordinary DRAM, not dual-port VRAM. Preserve independent refresh and bounded host access.

pixel_buffer.location: On video ASIC; SRAM banks with page ownership latches
pixel_buffer.policy: Eight-pixel parallel renderer fills free pages; independent clocked serializer drains ready pages. Two pages per 640-pixel line; prefill before active display; never overwrite displaying pages. Underflow blanks pixels, preserves sync and sets sticky fault.
pixel_buffer.physical_organization: Each 160-byte bank is 40 words × 32 bits. Load eight 4-bit pixels into a separate 32-bit serializer latch every eight dot clocks, then shift at 21.504 MHz. SRAM array reads run at 2.688 MHz, not one read per dot; filler and drain use different banks.

character_row_cache.purpose: Current and next 80-column character/attribute row; separate from 640-byte pixel FIFO.

timing_budget.qualification: Requalify existing renderer/FIFO and 16-bit DRAM organization for 640x400x2 and 640x200x4, refresh, sprite fetches, list prefetch and host/DMA stalls together. No greater upload throughput is promised by added capacity.

specification.arbitration: Card-local sequencer arbitrates display fetch and deadline-reserved independent DRAM refresh before bounded host/DMA transfers with READY. Sprite SRAM has its own 8-bit bus. System DMA/MMU remain dedicated host components; the card does not replace system-memory refresh.
specification.monitor_policy: All earlier modes and sprite/host/API features retained subject to monitor capabilities. assembly_requirements.description: Engineering baseline; electrical qualification, routing and supplier quotes pending.

specification.slot: One general 32-bit expansion slot; coexists with the dedicated primary video card
specification.mode_policy: Retain the June 64 KiB card text/bitmap modes and five-sprite behaviour, with explicit per-mode allocation and monitor capability checks. The 640x400x2 and 640x200x4 modes are inherited; 800x600x2 is the professional drawing mode.

palette_list.encoding: Byte 0: unsigned scanline delta; byte 1: palette-register index in high nibble, R in low nibble; byte 2: G in high nibble, B in low nibble. RGB components are 4 bits each.
palette_list.execution: Deltas accumulate from output active-line zero. Delta zero applies another write at the same boundary. Execute in preceding horizontal blank and latch before the target active line. Explicit count 0..512; a 10-bit count register avoids ambiguous terminators.
palette_list.long_gaps: Split gaps over 255 lines using harmless writes of an unchanged palette entry. These consume list entries.
palette_list.frame_state: Restore initial palette and reset list position at vertical blank. Software swaps or edits the active list only in a defined safe interval.
palette_list.write_limit: Design target at most four palette writes per output-line boundary, inherited from the June list budget; qualify transfer/settling against the faster raster before guaranteeing it. Reject over-budget lists rather than silently changing their timing.
palette_list.cad_policy: Static grayscale palette is the CAD default. Per-line palette changes are optional; 512 writes do not mean 512 distinct lines or 16 independent pixel shades in a 2bpp mode.

acceleration: Overlap-safe rectangle copies with stride and clipping
Rectangle fills and masked Boolean raster operations
Optional lookup-table antialiased lines with four output shades at 800x600
specification.redraw: Retain vector geometry; regenerate dirty regions and exposed pan strips. XOR may serve temporary simple cursors, not deletion of overlapping antialiased geometry. No 800x600 2bpp full-frame double buffering.
specification.sprites: Five legacy sprites use separate 1 KiB SRAM (two AION 2114 chips), outside the 128 KiB framebuffer/list allocation. Extend coordinate/addressing and line-budget validation to the 800x600 raster; no automatic sixth pointer sprite.
specification.monitor_modes: Mono Pro 17 uses a qualified fixed 800x600 raster. Older modes can be centered without scaling; the card reports presentation geometry and logical/output coordinate mapping. Older full-screen timings are enabled only for a monitor profile explicitly supporting them. No automatic multisync claim.
specification.host_integration: One general 32-bit Artemis slot for the additional professional card; the primary 64 KiB colour card keeps the dedicated video slot. Independent display handles, palettes, clocks, DMA/address resources and input focus.

composition_definition.role: Separate 1 KiB sprite SRAM; not charged against 128 KiB display RAM

memory_layout.mode_exclusivity: Text/font and bitmap allocations are alternative uses of 16 KiB display DRAM. The exclusive 1 KiB sprite SRAM remains available in every mode.
memory_layout.font_policy: One shared 2048-byte font; glyph edits affect both pages. Independent font buffering is not advertised in this baseline.
memory_layout.page_flip: Latch selected page during vertical blank; drawing throughput is not guaranteed by double buffering.

pixel_buffer.policy: FREE/FILLING/READY/READING banks; output latches and serializer. Never overwrite active bank; underrun preserves sync.

host_interface.implementation: Buffered 32-to-8-bit bridge with byte enables, staging latches and bounded READY/backpressure. Word uploads require up to four local transfers; no native 32-bit display-memory bank is claimed.

video.arbitration: Card-local sequencer arbitrates display fetch and deadline-reserved independent DRAM refresh before bounded host/DMA transfers with READY. Sprite SRAM has its own 8-bit bus. System DMA/MMU remain dedicated host components; the card does not replace system-memory refresh.
video.monitor_policy: Mono II / Color II use legacy 200-line raster profiles. No 26.88 kHz output and no Mono Pro support. CPU word size does not widen local display memory. All five sprites remain available.

memory_layout.mode_exclusivity: Text/font and bitmap allocations are alternative uses of 32 KiB display DRAM. Exclusive 1 KiB sprite SRAM is available in every mode.
memory_layout.font_policy: One shared 256-glyph bank per mode. Font allocation 2048 bytes at 8×8, 4096 at 8×16 or 8×10 (16-byte glyph stride). Font writes affect both pages.
memory_layout.page_flip: Latch selected page during vertical blank; drawing throughput is not guaranteed by double buffering.

display_memory.organization: 16K × 16 bits; ordinary external DRAM, independent display refresh sequencer.

pixel_buffer.location: On video ASIC; SRAM banks with page ownership latches
pixel_buffer.policy: Eight-pixel parallel renderer fills free pages; independent clocked serializer drains ready pages. Two pages per 640-pixel line; prefill before active display; never overwrite displaying pages. Underflow blanks pixels, preserves sync and sets sticky fault.
pixel_buffer.physical_organization: Each 160-byte bank is 40 words × 32 bits. Load eight 4-bit pixels into a separate 32-bit serializer latch every eight dot clocks, then shift at 21.504 MHz. SRAM array reads run at 2.688 MHz, not one read per dot; filler and drain use different banks.

character_row_cache.purpose: Current and next 80-column character/attribute row; separate from 640-byte pixel FIFO.

timing_budget.qualification: At 250 ns conservative DRAM cycle, 80 glyph fetches consume 20 microseconds per active line; 160-byte row prefetch amortizes across 8/10/16 scanlines. Two row caches and 16-bit reads cover text-row transitions. Verify sprites, refresh and bounded host/DMA slots together at voltage/temperature corners; no guaranteed maximum CPU upload rate.

video.arbitration: Card-local sequencer arbitrates display fetch and deadline-reserved independent DRAM refresh before bounded host/DMA transfers with READY. Sprite SRAM has its own 8-bit bus. System DMA/MMU remain dedicated host components; the card does not replace system-memory refresh.
video.monitor_policy: Read capability descriptor before enabling sync. Mono Pro accepts only raster_640_400; integer-scale legacy modes. Old monitors retain their advertised 200-line raster(s), never 640×400. Native 400-line modes require Mono Pro; new 200-line bitmap modes also work on capable older displays. This is display-mode/API compatibility, not Z80 binary compatibility.

networking.implementation: One removable NIC occupying one of the four general-purpose expansion slots; not additional integrated circuitry.
networking.rate_policy: Firmware-enforced host ceiling; actual common network rate also depends on every admitted station and qualified link.

memory.upgrade_policy: Use the shared module catalogue. Install matched pairs; preserve specified capacity. Replace all modules when changing density. Previous 16-bit population recipes are superseded.
memory.reliability_policy: No parity or ECC is fitted; any future parity design requires a separate qualified BOM.
memory.sourcing_policy: Qualified AION 64K×1 grades for 256 KB modules: 64/128 chips for the 512 KB/1 MB shipping capacities. The 768 KB target uses paired 128 KB two-rank 16K×1 modules. Shared interface and full-population qualification pending.

video.mode_discovery: Enumerate controller modes intersected with identified or configured monitor raster capabilities and available buffering/sprite allocations. Reject unsupported downscaling.

memory_layout.mode_exclusivity: Text/font and bitmap allocations are alternative uses of 32 KiB display DRAM. Exclusive 1 KiB sprite SRAM is available in every mode.
memory_layout.font_policy: One shared 256-glyph bank per mode. Font allocation 2048 bytes at 8×8, 4096 at 8×16 or 8×10 (16-byte glyph stride). Font writes affect both pages.
memory_layout.page_flip: Latch selected page during vertical blank; drawing throughput is not guaranteed by double buffering.

display_memory.organization: 16K × 16 bits; ordinary external DRAM, independent display refresh sequencer.

pixel_buffer.location: On video ASIC; SRAM banks with page ownership latches
pixel_buffer.policy: Eight-pixel parallel renderer fills free pages; independent clocked serializer drains ready pages. Two pages per 640-pixel line; prefill before active display; never overwrite displaying pages. Underflow blanks pixels, preserves sync and sets sticky fault.
pixel_buffer.physical_organization: Each 160-byte bank is 40 words × 32 bits. Load eight 4-bit pixels into a separate 32-bit serializer latch every eight dot clocks, then shift at 21.504 MHz. SRAM array reads run at 2.688 MHz, not one read per dot; filler and drain use different banks.

character_row_cache.purpose: Current and next 80-column character/attribute row; separate from 640-byte pixel FIFO.

timing_budget.qualification: At 250 ns conservative DRAM cycle, 80 glyph fetches consume 20 microseconds per active line; 160-byte row prefetch amortizes across 8/10/16 scanlines. Two row caches and 16-bit reads cover text-row transitions. Verify sprites, refresh and bounded host/DMA slots together at voltage/temperature corners; no guaranteed maximum CPU upload rate.

video.arbitration: Card-local sequencer arbitrates display fetch and deadline-reserved independent DRAM refresh before bounded host/DMA transfers with READY. Sprite SRAM has its own 8-bit bus. System DMA/MMU remain dedicated host components; the card does not replace system-memory refresh.
video.monitor_policy: Read capability descriptor before enabling sync. Mono Pro accepts only raster_640_400; integer-scale legacy modes. Old monitors retain their advertised 200-line raster(s), never 640×400. Native 400-line modes require Mono Pro; new 200-line bitmap modes also work on capable older displays. This is display-mode/API compatibility, not Z80 binary compatibility.

software_compatibility.adaptive_text: Applications query usable columns/rows instead of selecting behavior from model name.
software_compatibility.native_40_column_mode: Native 40×25 with 8×8 cells, plus all listed 80-column modes; discover via display API.

networking.implementation: One removable NIC occupying one of the four general-purpose expansion slots; not additional integrated circuitry.
networking.rate_policy: Firmware-enforced host ceiling; actual common network rate also depends on every admitted station and qualified link.

assembly_requirements.description: Remove 128 Kbit dependency

use four/eight high-density modules and two/four banks. Specify 8 MHz die/speed-bin and MMU timing, power and cooling at full population, exact HDD model and interface/format, network integration boundary, optional parity policy, RTC/battery need, and boot/service-console policy. Original server-only bundles exclude keyboard/monitor and still require validated headless operation or an optional console. New Mono Pro console bundles explicitly include both.
PCB dimensions, layer stack, finish, connectors, fitted passives and reference designators
Power per rail, startup/thermal limits and region-specific power configuration
Firmware image capacity/revision, programming and verification
Assembly routing, test fixtures, cycle times, yield/rework/scrap and packout
One replaceable video card is included in every chassis, on a dedicated connector, in addition to four general-purpose slots. Qualify 32 KiB DRAM, 1 KiB sprite SRAM and Mono Pro timings together.

data_interchange.vsam: Import host-exported sequential logical records from supported VSAM datasets using a supplied field/record layout. data_interchange.migration: Versioned document format; preserve supported older worksheets and reports. Older Abacus/Pulse editions must reject unsupported new features before writing. Explicit value-only export is a lossy interchange option.

acceptance_requirements: Measure memory, disk I/O, import/query/recalculation/report times and compression on named datasets.

abacus_file_integration.model: Read/edit/write Abacus document files; not live application integration.
abacus_file_integration.concurrency: Exclusive writer ownership. Do not edit a file concurrently in Pulse and Abacus.
abacus_file_integration.format_policy: Check format version and supported features before writing; reject unsupported edits without silently dropping data.
abacus_file_integration.save_policy: Write a replacement file, validate it, then perform a recoverable replacement retaining the prior version until success.
abacus_file_integration.formula_policy: Preserve formula text/encoding. Mark cached results invalid after edits; Abacus recalculates on opening unless Pulse has the matching evaluation library.
abacus_file_integration.memory_policy: Bounded record/cell iteration; whole-document duplication in RAM is not required.
abacus_file_integration.cross_version_policy: Each edition declares supported document-format versions. Later Artemis features are not implicitly writable by the Z80 edition.

before.name: AIONix 2 (ERA² edition)
before.description: ROM-backed successor to AIONix: protected preemptive multitasking, documented ERA ABI compatibility, recoverable HDD storage, user access management and an event-driven TUI designed for later graphical windowing.

rom_execution.mapping: Shared read-only executable mappings; private writable data per process. Cacheable ROM with independently qualified timing.
rom_execution.physical_implementation: At least 256 KiB of directly executable system ROM in the replaceable Athena system cartridge; physical BOM and host qualification belong to the cartridge device.

compatibility.scope: Documented ERA AIONix user binaries, instruction semantics and C ABI; not Z80 binary compatibility.
compatibility.mechanism: Executable ABI version selects legacy adapters; stable library dispatch and capability discovery.
compatibility.limits: Undocumented kernel dependencies, privileged drivers and direct hardware access require separate qualification; portable Z80 C applications require recompilation.

multitasking.kernel: Compact monolithic kernel; timer-preempted user processes, bounded non-preemptible kernel critical sections.
requirements: Fair scheduling with priority aging
Sleeping I/O and atomic sleep/wakeup
Checked user pointers and protected kernel/device mappings
Process-exit cleanup of files, memory, locks and child state
Per-process memory, file and request limits
Driver timeouts and bounded retries
Short interrupt handlers with deferred work
Responsive administrative termination path
Kernel-controlled DMA with checked pinned buffers
multitasking.limits: Process isolation does not isolate kernel/driver faults or independently constrain DMA. Fully preemptible kernel and application threads are not initial requirements.

initial_target: Consistent open/read/write/close/lseek/stat and descriptor duplication, inheritance and errors
Reliable existing copy-on-write fork, exec, wait, exit status and environment
Defined signal delivery, masks, dispositions and interrupted-call semantics
Canonical/raw terminal modes, terminal attributes and foreground process groups
Hierarchical paths, working directories, hard links and symbolic links
Pipes with EOF/broken-pipe semantics and readiness multiplexing
Shell quoting, redirection, pipelines, variables and exit statuses
Wall clock, monotonic elapsed time and explicit timestamp formats
later: Efficient spawn without replacing fork semantics
Broader file control and memory mapping
Broader utilities, locales, threads and timers
posix_direction.conformance: Publish per-interface implemented/partial/absent matrix and unsupported-operation errors; names alone do not establish conformance.

filesystem.design: Versioned inode-based filesystem; directory entries separate from metadata.
filesystem.qualification_note: Testing range, not capacity ceiling or a change to bundled HDD sizes.
requirements: Direct and indirect block pointers
Ownership, permissions, link counts and timestamps
Bounded metadata/data cache
Mount support and logical-sector driver interface with CHS translation when required
Clean/dirty volume state and consistency checker
Ordered metadata writes and explicit synchronization
Backup/restore utilities and defined durable-save ordering
filesystem.later: Small metadata journal after write-order and power-loss testing; journal does not by itself guarantee application-data durability.

initial_target: Numeric users and groups
Owner/group/other read/write/execute and directory search permissions
Creation masks
Real/effective credentials
Login sessions and home directories
Protected password database with salted costed hashing selected against CPU budget
Administrative control of devices, mounts and configuration
Kernel enforcement on all relevant operations
Protected administrative audit records
user_access.privilege: Qualify credential and exec transitions before enabling set-user-ID programs. Server authenticates identity rather than trusting client-supplied UID.
user_access.later: Extended ACLs and more elaborate policies.

ui_layers.name: Application layer
ui_layers.responsibility: Business logic and semantic commands such as Open, Save, Select and Cancel, independent of rendering.

ui_layers.name: Abstraction layer
ui_layers.responsibility: Events, menus, forms, lists, focus, layout, text measurement and drawing contexts.

ui_layers.name: Translation and compatibility layer
ui_layers.responsibility: Existing TUI adapters, terminal rendering, device backends and legacy ABI behavior; later graphical renderers.

ui_layers.name: OS native API
ui_layers.responsibility: Processes, files, IPC, timers, input devices and controlled display access.

ui_contract.implementation: Logical layers primarily in shared libraries plus a small UI service; not four mandatory processes or IPC crossings. Extend the existing portable C API.
initial_target: Unified bounded event queue for keys, timers, focus, redraw and future pointer events
Semantic commands separated from physical keys
Opaque window/view handles initially representing text regions
Clipping, invalidation and repaint requests
Layout constraints and explicit text measurement
Separate cell and pixel coordinates
Bounded clipboard and selection ownership
Capability/version discovery for graphics, fonts, color and pointer input
ui_contract.memory: Compact text state, dirty regions and redraw callbacks; no mandatory full-screen RAM backing bitmap.
ui_contract.next_generation: Windowed GUI; legacy character applications run in terminal windows. Adapters do not automatically redesign old UIs.

memory_management.initial: Shared ROM code, sparse page tables, small kernel stacks, reliable copy-on-write and graceful allocation failure.
memory_management.later: Controlled disk-backed paging/swap only after restart, locking and I/O qualification; keep fault handlers and essential paging state resident.
memory_management.policy: Swap handles occasional pressure, not a routinely oversized working set; ROM does not replace writable RAM.

qualification: Measured ROM/RAM footprint and Abacus/compiler/server workloads
TUI capability fallback and legacy terminal behavior

priority_assessment.feasibility: Strong existing foundation; fit and patch behavior must be measured.
Feasible with ERA protection and restart rules; extensive verification.
20–100 MB addressing is straightforward; crash recovery is the main risk.
Phase interfaces; full contemporary conformance excluded.
Depends on proven faults and I/O; not initial release gate.

release_scope.initial: ROM execution, documented legacy ABI, protected preemptive processes, recoverable HDD storage, users/permissions, POSIX-oriented subset and event-driven TUI groundwork.
release_scope.later: Paging/swap, metadata journal, broader networking/threads/locales and full windowed GUI.

resource_planning.basis: Engineering allocation target, not a measured fit or maximum. Server retains its existing 1 MiB configuration.

distribution.fulfillment: Software image supplied in the system cartridge fitted to every Athena; the physical cartridge contains this edition.
distribution.execution: At least 256 KiB directly executable shared OS ROM, alongside at least 256 KiB DRAM. EEPROM BIOS remains boot/diagnostic firmware. Optional services, larger utilities and patches load from disk; do not copy the entire OS ROM into RAM.
distribution.installation: Versioned dispatch tables and page-sized RAM patch overlays; ROM version/checksum checks and recovery boot bypassing disk patches. Patched pages consume DRAM. A qualified minor revision may be installed by exchanging the host-compatible cartridge; no specific future revision is asserted.

memory_management.initial: Shared ROM code, sparse page tables, small kernel stacks, reliable copy-on-write and graceful allocation failure.

memory_management.policy: Swap handles occasional pressure, not a routinely oversized working set; ROM does not replace writable RAM.

qualification: Measured ROM/RAM footprint and Abacus/compiler/server workloads

release_scope.initial: ROM execution, documented legacy ABI, protected preemptive processes, recoverable HDD storage, users/permissions, POSIX-oriented subset and event-driven TUI groundwork.

resource_planning.basis: Engineering allocation target, not a measured fit or maximum. Server retains its existing 1 MiB configuration.

distribution.fulfillment: Software image supplied in the system cartridge fitted to every Athena; the physical cartridge contains this edition.

implementation_design.title: BPI transactional client/server v1
implementation_design.architecture: Thin Z80/ERA clients send bounded business operations to an Artemis PRO server. Query evaluation, indexes, validation, accounting posting and transactions execute on the server; clients do not fetch arbitrary database pages.

transactions.concurrency: Single serialized writer for v1 with short transactions and bounded reader locks; no long interactive transaction while a user edits a form.
transactions.commit: Append checked log records and a commit marker, force them to durable storage, then acknowledge. Apply/replay committed changes idempotently.
transactions.recovery: On startup validate checksums and recover committed log records; incomplete transactions never become visible. Use shadow page/index replacement or another explicitly validated torn-write-safe method.
transactions.failure: Do not claim durable commit until disk/controller completion semantics are proven; no battery-backed cache is assumed.
transactions.log_format: Redo-only changed-record/page after-images with transaction ID, sequence, length and checksum; the commit marker covers transaction record count and checksum. Persist duplicate-suppression outcomes in the same transaction.
transactions.buffer_policy: Do not write uncommitted changes to database files (no-steal); cap transaction size to available transaction buffers.
transactions.checkpoint: Write replacement pages and indexes to new locations, force them, then alternate checksummed generation-numbered root/checkpoint records. Retain the preceding valid root and necessary redo log until the new checkpoint is durable.

protocol.transport: Length-framed requests over TCP; bounded messages and chunked results.
protocol.duplicate_suppression: Store committed write request IDs and outcomes durably. After reconnect, clients query status or retry with the same ID; never post the same payment twice.

data_integrity: Amounts use explicitly scaled integers/decimal rules, never unspecified binary floating-point rounding.
Record currency, rounding, posting dates, account periods and unique document IDs.
Cross-module posting is atomic and produces an append-only audit record.
operations: Backup captures a consistent checkpoint plus required logs; test restoration onto a clean disk.
Bounded log growth, disk-full handling and operator-visible recovery status
Plan backups and report traffic around the negotiated shared 100/250/500/1000 kbit/s raw LAN budget and measured payload throughput; slower admitted hosts limit the whole network.

initial_limits.client_policy: Bounded pages of results and forms; no entire-table download or whole-document duplication.

acceptance_tests: Full disk, corrupt log tail and failed backup restore

distribution.network_operation: Start under the existing networking OS, connect to server, and load further modules/data over the network; bootstrap remains local.
distribution.data_access: Business transactions, validation and database writes remain server-side; clients do not directly modify shared database files.

transactions.commit: Append checked log records and a commit marker, force them to durable storage, then acknowledge. Apply/replay committed changes idempotently.
transactions.recovery: On startup validate checksums and recover committed log records; incomplete transactions never become visible. Use shadow page/index replacement or another explicitly validated torn-write-safe method.
transactions.failure: Do not claim durable commit until disk/controller completion semantics are proven; no battery-backed cache is assumed.
transactions.log_format: Redo-only changed-record/page after-images with transaction ID, sequence, length and checksum; the commit marker covers transaction record count and checksum. Persist duplicate-suppression outcomes in the same transaction.
transactions.buffer_policy: Do not write uncommitted changes to database files (no-steal); cap transaction size to available transaction buffers.
transactions.checkpoint: Write replacement pages and indexes to new locations, force them, then alternate checksummed generation-numbered root/checkpoint records. Retain the preceding valid root and necessary redo log until the new checkpoint is durable.

protocol.transport: Length-framed requests over TCP; bounded messages and chunked results.
protocol.duplicate_suppression: Store committed write request IDs and outcomes durably. After reconnect, clients query status or retry with the same ID; never post the same payment twice.

data_integrity: Amounts use explicitly scaled integers/decimal rules, never unspecified binary floating-point rounding.
Record currency, rounding, posting dates, account periods and unique document IDs.
Cross-module posting is atomic and produces an append-only audit record.
operations: Backup captures a consistent checkpoint plus required logs; test restoration onto a clean disk.
Bounded log growth, disk-full handling and operator-visible recovery status
Plan backups and report traffic around the negotiated shared 100/250/500/1000 kbit/s raw LAN budget and measured payload throughput; slower admitted hosts limit the whole network.

before.description: Separately offered 16 KB XIP ROM expansion cartridge with four applications: text editor, disk browser, calculator and calendar/scheduler. It calls TUI & services in the CP/M system cartridge. It does not contain a duplicate shared TUI library; application documents and state occupy RAM or disk storage.

subcomponents.name: Text editor
subcomponents.description: Own text documents and editor commands, using the system editing controls, screen services and clipboard.

subcomponents.name: Disk browser
subcomponents.description: Own disk/file browsing workflows, using system list controls, dialogs and file services.

subcomponents.name: Calculator
subcomponents.description: Own arithmetic operations and calculator state, using system input fields and clipboard services.

subcomponents.name: Calendar / scheduler
subcomponents.description: Own calendar records and scheduling workflows, using system forms, navigation and display services.

runtime_notes: The cartridge remains a 16 KB product capacity; removing duplicate routines does not establish a measured free-space budget.
Uses one cartridge slot alongside the CP/M system cartridge.
Code executes from banked ROM where practical; writable application state is held in RAM.
Reusable TUI widgets, screen and input primitives, clipboard ownership and workspace mechanisms belong to the CP/M system cartridge.
Application-specific text editing, file browsing, calculation and scheduling logic remain in this cartridge.
The applications call the system TUI interface; they do not require their own copy of its library.
A resident workspace reserves RAM explicitly; the cartridge does not imply multitasking.

before.name: Aurelia Software Compatibility Kit (CP/M edition)
before.description: Manufacturer and independent-integrator kit for implementing the released Aurelia application environment on independently designed computers.

contents: Published processor, CP/M, memory, display, keyboard, storage and error-behaviour contracts
Reference runtime adapter source and redistribution terms
Diagnostics and conformance tests, including resource limits and failure cases
Abacus and Business Tools acceptance workloads: calculations, file interchange, printing, save/reopen
Porting and troubleshooting manuals, source listings and machine-readable disks
Versioned results forms and optional certification submission requirements

compatibility_policy.eligibility: Any manufacturer or independent integrator may implement the published environment without a bespoke partnership or mandatory certification.
compatibility_policy.binary: Existing Z80 binaries require compatible instruction execution and the specified OS/runtime and memory behaviour; CP/M alone is insufficient. Other processors need an appropriate port or execution solution.
compatibility_policy.hardware: Native video, keyboards, disks and printers may be exposed through adapters. FlexiBUS and Logix video hardware are separate optional profiles. Full hardware clones may implement those published interfaces under their applicable terms.
compatibility_policy.applications: Named supported platforms are tested configurations, not an exclusive permission list. Independently implemented environments may run properly licensed applications; certification identifies precisely what AION tested.
compatibility_policy.delivery: Printed manuals/source listings and disks; host/media conversion quoted separately.
compatibility_policy.certification: Optional, configuration- and version-specific. Manufacturer-declared compatibility is distinct from AION-tested application compatibility. FlexiBUS electrical/protocol and Logix display tests are separate claims.

before.description: One Artemis PRO server entitlement and four concurrent network developer sessions. Hardware, network adapters, hub and backup media sold separately. C IDE version 2 runs locally after network loading; shared source/results live on the server.

features: Repository: atomic multi-file commits, author/date/message, branches, release labels, diffs, rollback and comments tied to immutable revisions; isolated workspaces, saving is not committing
Collaboration: text channels, posts and replies with file/revision/commit references; shared calendar, meetings, invitations, tasks, owners, deadlines and milestones
C Development Environment 2: local Artemis ERA/Z80 builds; compact Aurelia/Aurelia+ TUI and local Z80 tools; queued server ERA/heavy builds
Initial targets CP/M/Z80 and AIONix/ERA with separate binaries, startup code and libraries; Breakthru TUI portability layer and target adapters
Reproducible builds record source revisions, compiler versions, build settings and target libraries
Network loader uses bounded transfers; acknowledged saves and recoverable workspaces after disconnect
Apple and Commodore target packages are future roadmap work; no launch support or binary compatibility claim

specification.server: Artemis PRO, recommended 1 MiB; existing 5 MB disk supports bounded pilot projects only. Archive old history and rotate external floppy backups; larger qualified storage required for substantial projects and is not bundled or priced here.
specification.clients: Artemis, Aurelia and Aurelia+ with network upgrade; Aurelia compact tools use sequential overlays within its CP/M memory profile. No full suite resident in 48 KiB claim.
specification.qualification: Four concurrent developers is a validation target, not measured throughput. Gate release on commit recovery, access control, backup/restore, conflict handling and both target regression suites.
specification.sponsored_deployment: Sponsor supplies hardware, qualified concurrency/storage and dedicated support beyond retail caps; retail entitlement remains unchanged.

adoption_pricing.scope: No automatic expiry or second compounded reduction.
adoption_pricing.rationale: Preserve one server/four concurrent users, 20h onboarding, 12h first-year support, media and documentation. Hardware remains separate.
adoption_pricing.loss_treatment: Show actual negative unit contribution after dealer fees. Do not add the same shortfall a second time as a marketing expense in a future P&L.
